newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power output dips 0.2 pct vs. year ago - EEI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power output dips 0.2 pct vs. year ago - EEI.

text.p: Electricity deliveries in the continental U.S. totaled 59,531 gigawatt hours (GWh) for the week ended October 5, down 0.2 percent from the same period in 1995, the Edison Electric Institute (EEI) said.
The amount of power supplied to the Rocky Mountain region rose the most from a year ago in the latest reporting week, up 11.3 percent to 3,207 GWh.
The Pacific Northwest saw the largest decline from the corresponding period in 1995, down 4.8 percent to 3,049 GWh.
Year-to-date domestic power production totaled about 2.57 million GWh, up 2.2 percent from the same period in 1995, EEI said.
